solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having become suddenly interested, son exercises

parts.note: to sit up (and take notice) is to become suddenly alert and interested
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A boy, suddenly keen, starts doing his gym routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'sit up and take notice' supplies the idea of becoming suddenly interested; the tense of the clue's phrase is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises done by raising the trunk from lying flat.

clue.text: Team members producing weapons

parts.note: a side is a sports team
arms are limbs, which are bodily members

explanation.surface: Players on a squad produce guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' looks like team players, but it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are weapons, such as pistols, worn at the side.

clue.text: Mean to hold on this evening

indicators.note: the word for mean wraps around the next piece, holding it

parts.note: tight is slang for stingy, or mean with money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone intends to keep going until later today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, to intend; it is the adjective for stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening of the present day.

clue.text: Quiet, living in a place such as Cleveland?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
a resident is someone living in a particular place

explanation.surface: Someone lives quietly in a city like Cleveland, Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleveland looks like the US city; it is Grover Cleveland, a US head of state, hence the question mark for a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland served twice as head of state of the USA.

clue.text: In pairs, making four

definitions.meaning: going along two at a time, as the animals entered the ark
the multiplication two times two gives four

explanation.definitionFit: Two by two describes walking in pairs and is also the sum that equals four.

clue.text: Satanic ritual, perhaps, with short game seaman on tub

indicators.note: the word with is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: chess is a board game
AB is an able-bodied seaman
a bath is a tub

explanation.surface: A sailor sits on a bathtub playing a short game during a devilish rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tub' and 'seaman' paint a sailor scene, but each is a plain synonym; 'on' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A midnight gathering of witches, supposedly to worship the devil, is a Satanic ritual, perhaps.

clue.text: Mineral artist poured into carton

indicators.note: the artist's letters are put inside the container word

parts.note: a box is a carton
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is crammed into a cardboard box with a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Borax is a white mineral, a salt of boron used in cleaning products.

clue.text: Set off in time ahead of scaffolder

indicators.note: the time letter comes before the scaffolder

parts.note: a rigger erects scaffolding or rigging

explanation.surface: A scaffold worker leaves before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing, but it means to cause or start something.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, as an alarm.

clue.text: Performing well in lessons on green

indicators.note: in shows that the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Doing nicely in lessons on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: ON SONG is British slang for being in top form.
explanation.definitionFit: On song is a British idiom meaning playing or working at one's best.

clue.text: In a straight line? Amazing cartwheels, if so

indicators.note: amazing suggests a maze of letters, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonderful gymnastic cartwheels, but only if they go straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CARTWHEELS IF SO gives the phrase; the question mark marks a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the most direct route between two places describes the path a bird takes.

clue.text: Concealed, group meeting after reverend's last service

indicators.note: the following pieces come after and join the opening letter
the clue asks for the final letter of the word reverend

parts.note: inner can mean private or hidden from view
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Something secret happens after the vicar's final church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks ecclesiastical next to 'reverend', but it means a set of matching tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: A service in the crockery sense is a full matching set of plates and dishes.

clue.text: Rex lends a hand in more than one attack

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures
to aid is to lend a hand, so lends a hand gives aids

explanation.surface: A king helps out in a series of assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Raids are sudden attacks, and the plural answers to more than one attack.

clue.text: Wilt, when lead's lost, causing anxiety

indicators.note: the leading letter of the synonym for wilt is removed

parts.note: to languish is to droop or wilt

explanation.surface: A plant drooping after losing its leader causes worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilt Chamberlain may come to mind, but 'Wilt' is a verb meaning to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental distress, a strong form of anxiety.

clue.text: Jinx a reportedly spent figure

parts.note: a hex is a curse or jinx

indicators.note: signals that the word for spent is used for its sound only

parts.note: something spent or used up is gone

explanation.surface: A curse is said to have used up some shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexagon is a geometrical figure with six sides.

clue.text: One identifies bishop and rook pocketed by small child

indicators.note: the rook's letter goes inside the word for a small child, as if in its pocket

parts.note: a mite is a small child
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A little one pockets chess pieces, a bishop and a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess context of 'bishop and rook' is misleading: the bishop is a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is recognised by the tall pointed headdress he wears, his mitre.

clue.text: Money to come by sheer fine wool

parts.note: cash is ready money
sheer and mere both mean nothing other than, as in a sheer or mere coincidence

explanation.surface: Money will come to buy some fine wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is the soft fine wool from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Fashion garment thrown together

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: Designing clothing quickly assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the clothing trade; it is the verb meaning to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift means improvised or hastily put together as a temporary measure.

clue.text: Unnecessary to bug steamship

parts.note: to needle is to bug or irritate

explanation.surface: No need to plant a listening device on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not needed, the same as unnecessary.

clue.text: The polar winds in abundance

indicators.note: winds as a verb means twists about, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Arctic winds blow in great numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like a noun for polar gales; it is the verb that rearranges THE POLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or superabundance of something.

clue.text: Alas, alas — English served up Continental dish

indicators.note: the second alas, an exclamation of dismay, signals the first is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A Brit sighs over foreign food being served.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'alas' is the anagram signal for the first, making LASA; 'served up' reverses ENG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian dish of layered pasta, from the European mainland.

clue.text: Card, king, Welshman rejected

parts.note: K is the card and chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A king is turned away by a man from Wales during a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns EVAN into NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the playing card otherwise called the jack.

clue.text: A staunch worker refusing to be persuaded

parts.note: to staunch is to stem a flow, as a dam does
a worker is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A loyal employee will not change their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective for loyal; it is the verb meaning to stem a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means firmly unyielding in one's opinion.

clue.text: Something as yet undeveloped — more by rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Something not yet grown, more is left beside the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism or idea at its earliest, undeveloped stage.

clue.text: Old lady's pet dog

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, so MA, with the possessive S
a pet is a fit of sulking, like a tiff or quarrel

explanation.surface: Mother's favourite animal is a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal; it means a fit of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Opening number covered by jazzy trio

indicators.note: the number's letter is put inside the rearranged group of three
jazzy suggests livening up the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: The first piece is played by a lively jazz trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazzy' rearranges TRIO to ITRO, and 'covered by' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Something like a crane's terribly bad rust

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A crane is covered in horrible rust.
explanation.walkthrough: The crane looks like construction machinery, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustard is a large long-legged ground bird, crane-like in build.

clue.text: Sound cheerful after opener's dismissed

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym is removed, as an opening batsman is out in cricket

parts.note: bright means cheerful and lively

explanation.surface: A cheery noise after the opening batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise; it is the adjective for well-founded or correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and sound both mean correct or well-founded, as in a sound judgement.

clue.text: Involved in endless attempts to catch pet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the shortened attempts surround the pet, catching it
the last letter of the word for attempts is dropped

parts.note: tries are attempts
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: Someone is caught up in repeated efforts to trap an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' sits at the front looking like part of the surface, but it is the definition; the 'in' after it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means complicated or involved, with many interconnected parts.

clue.text: Small, like some carriages?

definitions.meaning: a ... town is small and insignificant
some carriages are drawn by a single horse

explanation.definitionFit: One-horse means minor or petty, and literally describes a single-horse carriage.

clue.text: Class, say, mostly American

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for say is dropped, leaving most of it

parts.note: to say is to state
US is short for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: Talk about class, mostly American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts STATE to STAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means social standing or rank, which is one's class.
